title: Account for every point of feedback
statement: Map every point of feedback on its own to a decision and its evidence, and never drop one or bury it in a bulk statement that feedback was addressed.
detail: The standard's golden checklist asks whether every point raised in review is individually accounted for: each source point needs a disposition and links to one or more requirements and exact evidence, so that nothing material is lost behind a bulk statement that feedback was addressed (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q002). The 1.0 standard names bulk 'addressed' claims, missing source points and evidence with no feedback link as its failure signals (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`), and the base red-team profile maps each point to criteria and evidence and says feedback is neither dropped nor silently promoted into universal policy (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/profiles/base/RED_TEAM_BASE.source.json`).
against: Mapping a point is not accepting it: each linked requirement still needs its own evidence (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`).
